subject: Data custodianship & access pathways — post-demo clarifications
messages:

Subject: Data custodianship & access pathways — post-demo clarifications

Hi Priya / Tom,

Thanks again for hopping on the demo earlier — great conversation. As promised, a short recap of the items we discussed around data custodianship and how that maps to Redwood deployment choices (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). I also noted a few clarifying questions so we can pull the right people into the next security deep-dive.

Quick recap (call highlights):
- Primary concern: strict logical separation of customer data and control-plane access; Medsys requires limited third-party access to request/response data and strong KMS controls.
- Options we discussed:
  • Hosted API: fastest to go-live, but data flows through Redwood-managed control plane (not a fit if you need customer-managed KMS or zero-external-operator-access).
  • Dedicated (reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools and tenant isolation for inference; control plane still Redwood-managed but can be configured to minimize logs and enable strong auditing.
  • Private VPC / on-prem: private control plane (or on-prem package) with customer-managed networking, optional BYOK/HSM, and no Redwood operator access unless explicitly permitted.

Clarifying questions for your security team (so we can prepare the right artefacts):
1) Who is Medsys’ formal data custodian for this workload (name & email)?
2) Do you require customer-managed keys (BYOK in HSM)? If yes, which vendor (AWS KMS/CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault, other)?
3) Level of access requested for vendor (Redwood) personnel for debugging — 0 / readonly-sanitized-logs / timeboxed elevated access?
4) Any specific egress/network controls or private peering requirements we should pre-validate?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vpc-checklist.pdf (summary of differences and controls), proposed-mop-v1.xlsx (draft mutual action plan).

Suggested next steps:
- If you can confirm the points above, we’ll schedule a 60-minute security deep-dive (include your infra/security/PCI folks) and bring our Private deployments PM + infra engineer.
- I’ll also attach a short custodianship matrix showing what we can enable in each deployment mode.

Thanks — happy to adjust wording for your SSO/KMS folks.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-26T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Data custodianship & access pathways — post-demo clarifications

Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from Security before we lock in a deep-dive: 

1) BYOK is a hard requirement for any production inference of PHI — we need customer-managed keys in an HSM (CloudHSM preferred).
2) No persistent access to raw request/response logs by any vendor is allowed. Timeboxed, audited access for incident response is acceptable.
3) For Dedicated — does Redwood offer an option where the control plane is logically separated, and can we have a guaranteed SLA for purging cache/KV material at termination?

I’ve attached our security questionnaire for the moment — it’s partially filled by our security team (security-questionnaire.pdf). We’ll aim to get the named data custodian and a few network contacts to you by EOD.

Regards,
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Security, Medsys Health
tom.ellis@medsys.com | +1 (617) 555-0091

Subject: Re: Data custodianship & access pathways — post-demo clarifications

Tom — really appreciate the specifics, that helps a lot. Short answers (and what we’ll bring to the security deep-dive):

- BYOK/HSM: Supported. For Private VPC and on-prem packages we support BYOK integrations (AWS KMS + CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault). We can validate proof-of-keys flow and key rotation policy with your KMS team ahead of install.

- Logs & vendor access: We can operate under a policy of zero persistent retention of raw request/response logs for production if you choose Private VPC. For Dedicated, we offer configurable retention windows and an option to redact or not persist user inputs at the token level. Timeboxed, auditable operator access is supported for incident response; we require mutual approval and provide full audit logs (who/when/why).

- Control plane separation & purge guarantees:
  • Dedicated: tenant-isolated inference runtime + dedicated GPU pools. The control plane is Redwood-managed; however, for dedicated customers we can provide contract language on cache purge on termination and an architecture diagram showing logical separation. We can also include an automated KV purge hook as part of the teardown process.
  • Private VPC / on-prem: full customer-managed control plane option. No Redwood operator access by default; all keys remain in your KMS/HSM and we can supply build/config automation for key provisioning without transmitting key material to Redwood.

Attached: custodianship-matrix.csv (mapping of controls across deployment modes). I added a proposed mutual action plan itemization at the bottom of the matrix:
- M1: Security deep-dive (60m) — Redwood infra + Private deployments PM + your security + KMS admin
- M2: Proof-of-concept (2 weeks) — Private VPC staging, BYOK integration, SSO/SAML test accounts
- M3: Contract addendum — BYOK + purge SLA + operator access policy (timeboxed)

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Wed 2027-04-28 10:00–11:00 PDT or Thu 2027-04-29 13:00–14:00 PDT. Which works for your team?

If you want we can also prepare a short runbook showing what data types Redwood logs in each mode (control-plane telemetry vs customer payload) and the exact vetting process for operator access.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
